info.name: Orchard Floor
info.text: Hard earth and dry grass under the trees. Every fallen fruit is counted and every missing one is somebody's fault.

info.name: Orchard Floor B
info.text: Windfall rotting in the dust. The overseer calls it waste, the slaves call it lunch.

info.name: Orchard Floor (basket)
info.text: A tipped basket and a single sandal. The picker left in a hurry, the overseer followed with a stick.

info.name: Bean and Lentil Beds
info.text: Beans, lentils and chickpeas: the soldier's meal, the slave's meal, the senator's secret meal.

info.name: Bean and Lentil Beds B
info.text: Lentils in the sun. Cheap, filling and a reliable cause of unrest in the barracks.

info.name: Physic Garden
info.text: Square beds of sage, rue, rosemary and marigold. Half of them heal, the other half are for inheritance matters.

info.name: Physic Garden (label)
info.text: A little wooden label nobody can read anymore. The physician swears it said "not for soup".

info.name: Lavender Field
info.text: Purple rows that smell of luxury. The bath houses need a lot of it to hide what they smell of.

info.name: Lavender Field
info.text: Purple rows that smell of luxury. The bath houses need a lot of it to hide what they smell of.

info.name: Poppy Field
info.text: Pale poppies with scratched seed heads. The milk that drips out makes even the arena bearable.

info.name: Poppy Field (knife)
info.text: A small knife left among the capsules. The harvester took a nap. A long one.

info.name: Poppy Field

info.name: Poppy Field (knife)
info.text: A small knife left among the capsules. The harvester took a nap. A long one.

info.name: Pen
info.text: Trampled mud, old straw and a puddle that never dries. Home sweet home for goats, donkeys and chickens.

info.name: Pen (trough)
info.text: A feeding trough with a few wisps of hay. The animals eat first; the stable boy eats what is left.

info.name: Vineyard Soil
info.text: Hoed earth between the vines, mulched with straw. Wine starts here, in the dirt, like most fortunes.

info.name: Vineyard Soil B
info.text: Yellow leaves and trampled grapes. It looks like a massacre, and it is only the harvest.

info.name: Saffron Field
info.text: Crocus flowers picked one by one for three red threads each. Worth more than the hands that pick them.

info.name: Saffron Field
info.text: Crocus flowers picked one by one for three red threads each. Worth more than the hands that pick them.

info.name: Pasture
info.text: Grass grazed short, a sheep path and the usual droppings. The sheep are counted daily, the shepherds only when missing.

info.name: Pasture B
info.text: Close-cropped grass. Sheep eat it, wolves eat the sheep, the landlord eats the shepherd's wages.

info.name: Pasture (thistles)
info.text: Thistles the sheep refuse to eat. Smart sheep.

info.name: Pasture (salt lick)
info.text: A salt stone licked smooth. Salt is so dear that the sheep are paid better than the legion.

info.name: Pasture (lost bell)
info.text: A sheep bell with a torn strap. The sheep is gone. The shepherd is next, once the owner finds out.

info.name: Wheat Field
info.text: Golden wheat in neat rows. It feeds the city, the city feeds the arena, the arena feeds on the city.

info.name: Wheat Field B
info.text: Wheat waving politely. The tax collector already counted every ear.

info.name: Wheat Field (trampled)
info.text: Someone ran straight through the wheat. Debtors rarely take the road.

info.name: Wheat Field (crows)
info.text: The crows took their share before the landlord could. Only the feathers paid tax.

info.name: Wheat Field (sickle)
info.text: A sickle left in the stubble, a dark stain beside it. Harvest accidents are counted as harvest.

info.name: Boulder
info.text: A grey boulder that has not moved since the gods dropped it. Patient, silent and completely useless until someone brings a pickaxe.

info.name: Rock Terrace
info.text: The hill under the important people. It holds them up better than the people below do.

info.name: Rock Terrace
info.text: Bare rock, one step higher. Down here you pay rent, up there you collect it.

info.name: Rock Stairs
info.text: Cut into the hill by convicts, worn smooth by priests, slippery for everybody else.

info.name: Fighting Pit
info.text: A sunken square of bloody sand and a ladder. The ladder only goes one way for most.

info.name: Worker
info.text: An ordinary man of the ludus in a simple tunic. He carries, saws and digs until the day somebody hands him a sword instead.

info.name: Upturned Boat
info.text: A fishing boat keel-up on trestles, a pot of tar beside it. Boats are tarred every spring and prayed for every storm.

info.name: Patched Boat
info.text: A hole in the hull, half nailed over with a plank. The plank came from the last boat, which also had a hole.

info.name: Net Rack
info.text: Nets drying on two poles, with cork floats and a tear nobody will admit to. Mending is women's work, said a man once.

info.text: A small treading basin by the threshing floor. The master gets the wine, the workers get purple feet.

info.name: Chopping Block
info.text: Block, maul and a pile of split firewood. The block has been hit more times than any gladiator alive.

info.name: Log Pile
info.text: Trimmed logs held by stakes. Pull the wrong stake and the pile becomes the fastest thing in the camp.

info.name: Saw Buck
info.text: A log on the saw buck, a crosscut saw on the ground and a carpet of sawdust. Two men, one rhythm, frequent arguments.

info.name: Trap Pile
info.text: Two cages, a coil of snares and a deadfall on its trigger stick. Step around it; the last apprentice did not.

info.name: Hide Frame
info.text: A hide laced into a frame and a scraping beam. Somewhere a forest is one animal lighter and the arena one costume richer.

info.name: Smoking Rack
info.text: Strips of meat over a cold fire pit. The hunter smokes the meat, the meat smokes the hunter, and both end up leathery.

info.name: Ox Cart
info.text: A cart with one ox and three sacks. The ox does the work and the driver takes the credit; the ox is used to it.

info.name: Charcoal Heap
info.text: Fresh charcoal, light and black. It weighs a fifth of the wood it was and costs five times as much.

info.name: Turf and Water
info.text: Earth and turf to smother the kiln, and a barrel of water for the rest. The barrel is for the kiln; the burner can wait.

info.name: Charcoal Kiln
info.text: A dome of wood under earth and turf, smouldering for days. If it breathes too hard, the burner breathes too little.

info.name: Kiln Burnt Through
info.text: The kiln burnt through on one side and has been patched with fresh turf. The shovel stayed where it fell.

info.name: Kiln Being Built
info.text: Billets stacked around the centre pole like a tent of firewood. In a week it will be a sack of charcoal.

info.name: Charcoal Sacks
info.text: Sacks of charcoal and a tally stick. The buyer counts the sacks, the burner counts the notches; neither agrees.

info.name: Royal Banner Blank
info.text: The royal banner. The crown was unpicked when the last king fell; the next one has not decided yet how big his should be.

info.name: Royal Banner Blank I
info.text: The royal banner. The crown was unpicked when the last king fell; the next one has not decided yet how big his should be.

info.name: Royal Palace N
info.text: Behind the throne room the king feasts in his garden. The cage is empty; the lion is out, doing what lions and kings do best.

info.name: Royal Palace W
info.text: A golden gladiator on a modest plinth, propped up by two beams. The king says it is him. Nobody has said otherwise twice.

info.name: Royal Palace
info.text: Built by thousands, enjoyed by one. Petitions are accepted at the gate and answered next year, every year.

info.name: Royal Palace E
info.text: The dome is gold where the money lasted and bronze where it did not. The east wing waits for the next tax.

info.name: Storage Spot
info.text: A pallet with crates and a sack. Everything here belongs to somebody, and that somebody is not the man carrying it.

info.name: Storage Spot A
info.text: Two barrels and a crate. One holds wine, one holds vinegar, and the label fell off years ago.

info.name: Storage Spot B
info.text: Grain sacks and an amphora. The weevils got here first and are not paying rent.

info.name: Storage Spot C
info.text: Firewood stacked by someone who will never be warm.

info.name: Storage Spot D
info.text: A crate of skulls, sorted by size. The arena sells everything, eventually.

info.name: Storage Spot E
info.text: Spare chains and a sack of grain with a rat on top. The rat lost the negotiation.

info.name: Corpse
info.text: A fallen gladiator in a dark puddle. He lies here for a day so the next ones know what the purse costs; then the cart takes him.

info.name: Slave Market
info.text: The slave trader's stall. Every morning he brings five new men in chains; whoever is left at dusk goes back on the road with him. No refunds.

info.name: Animal Goods Stall
info.text: Empty cages, a basket of eggs, a bale of wool. The cages were full this morning. Nobody asks where it all went.

info.name: Animal Goods Double Stall N
info.text: Two butchers who share one stall and one cleaver. Whatever one of them sells, the other one is still looking for.

info.name: Animal Goods Double Stall E
info.text: Two butchers who share one stall and one cleaver. Whatever one of them sells, the other one is still looking for.

info.name: Animal Goods Double Stall S
info.text: Two butchers who share one stall and one cleaver. Whatever one of them sells, the other one is still looking for.

info.name: Animal Goods Double Stall W
info.text: Two butchers who share one stall and one cleaver. Whatever one of them sells, the other one is still looking for.

info.name: Animal Goods Market Tent N
info.text: A tent full of hides, bones, sausages and empty cages. EVERY PART, says the board. Except the part that ran off.

info.name: Animal Goods Market Tent E
info.text: A tent full of hides, bones, sausages and empty cages. EVERY PART, says the board. Except the part that ran off.

info.name: Animal Goods Market Tent S
info.text: A tent full of hides, bones, sausages and empty cages. EVERY PART, says the board. Except the part that ran off.

info.name: Animal Goods Market Tent W
info.text: A tent full of hides, bones, sausages and empty cages. EVERY PART, says the board. Except the part that ran off.

info.name: Animal Goods Stall B
info.text: Hides nailed to the back, a basket of bones and a few horns. Everything but the animal, and the soup is made of that.

info.name: Animal Goods Stall C
info.text: Sausages, a bloody block and pots of fat. The board says MEAT?, which is the most honest thing in the market.

info.name: Animal Goods Stall D
info.text: A big cage, bars bent outward, a torn chain. The sign says GONE. The vendor is looking for a new arm and a new bear.

info.name: Arena Supply Stall
info.text: Sacks of fresh arena sand, rakes and red-rimmed buckets. Sand soaks up anything, so they sell a lot of it.

info.name: Arena Supply Double Stall N
info.text: Sand on one side, coffins on the other. The lanistas buy both in one trip and save a walk.

info.name: Arena Supply Double Stall E
info.text: Sand on one side, coffins on the other. The lanistas buy both in one trip and save a walk.

info.name: Arena Supply Double Stall S
info.text: Sand on one side, coffins on the other. The lanistas buy both in one trip and save a walk.

info.name: Arena Supply Double Stall W
info.text: Sand on one side, coffins on the other. The lanistas buy both in one trip and save a walk.

info.name: Arena Supply Market Tent N
info.text: Coffins at the back, hooks in the middle, wreaths at the counter. The tent is laid out like a career.

info.name: Arena Supply Market Tent E
info.text: Coffins at the back, hooks in the middle, wreaths at the counter. The tent is laid out like a career.

info.name: Arena Supply Market Tent S
info.text: Coffins at the back, hooks in the middle, wreaths at the counter. The tent is laid out like a career.

info.name: Arena Supply Market Tent W
info.text: Coffins at the back, hooks in the middle, wreaths at the counter. The tent is laid out like a career.

info.name: Arena Supply Stall B
info.text: Coffins, stacked and priced by the dozen. BULK, says the board. Lanistas never buy just one.

info.name: Arena Supply Stall C
info.text: Nets, chains, a stretcher and drag hooks for the Gate of Death. Hooks are the bestseller; nets come back broken.

info.name: Arena Supply Stall D
info.text: One victory wreath, five coffins. The board says ODDS and the stock agrees.

info.name: Arms & Armour Stall
info.text: Swords on a rack, dented shields and plumed helmets. USED, says the board. By whom is not mentioned.

info.name: Arms & Armour Double Stall N
info.text: Two smiths, one table, a long row of blades. BARELY USED: the previous owners barely got to use them.

info.name: Arms & Armour Double Stall E
info.text: Two smiths, one table, a long row of blades. BARELY USED: the previous owners barely got to use them.

info.name: Arms & Armour Double Stall S
info.text: Two smiths, one table, a long row of blades. BARELY USED: the previous owners barely got to use them.

info.name: Arms & Armour Double Stall W
info.text: Two smiths, one table, a long row of blades. BARELY USED: the previous owners barely got to use them.

info.name: Arms & Armour Market Tent N
info.text: A tent of dented helmets, broken shields and swords with stories. WAR SURPLUS, though nobody remembers which war.

info.name: Arms & Armour Market Tent E
info.text: A tent of dented helmets, broken shields and swords with stories. WAR SURPLUS, though nobody remembers which war.

info.name: Arms & Armour Market Tent S
info.text: A tent of dented helmets, broken shields and swords with stories. WAR SURPLUS, though nobody remembers which war.

info.name: Arms & Armour Market Tent W
info.text: A tent of dented helmets, broken shields and swords with stories. WAR SURPLUS, though nobody remembers which war.

info.name: Arms & Armour Stall B
info.text: Spears in a barrel and a grindstone. Every blade sharpened on site, so the first owner never knew what hit him.

info.name: Arms & Armour Stall C
info.text: Breastplates and a heap of rings that used to be mail. Half price, because half of the last owner is still inside.

info.name: Arms & Armour Stall D
info.text: A helmet with a neat hole, a bloody sword and a broken one. MINT, says the board. A brave vendor.

info.name: Clothing Stall
info.text: Tunics on a line, folded linen and a pair of sandals. All second-hand. The first hand did not need them any more.

info.name: Clothing Double Stall N
info.text: Tunics on two lines and a lot of linen. WASHED TWICE, says the board. Once was not enough.

info.name: Clothing Double Stall E
info.text: Tunics on two lines and a lot of linen. WASHED TWICE, says the board. Once was not enough.

info.name: Clothing Double Stall S
info.text: Tunics on two lines and a lot of linen. WASHED TWICE, says the board. Once was not enough.

info.name: Clothing Double Stall W
info.text: Tunics on two lines and a lot of linen. WASHED TWICE, says the board. Once was not enough.

info.name: Clothing Market Tent N
info.text: A tent of tunics with neat holes and a tub of pink water. ESTATE SALE: the estates are freshly buried.

info.name: Clothing Market Tent E
info.text: A tent of tunics with neat holes and a tub of pink water. ESTATE SALE: the estates are freshly buried.

info.name: Clothing Market Tent S
info.text: A tent of tunics with neat holes and a tub of pink water. ESTATE SALE: the estates are freshly buried.

info.name: Clothing Market Tent W
info.text: A tent of tunics with neat holes and a tub of pink water. ESTATE SALE: the estates are freshly buried.

info.name: Clothing Stall B
info.text: Bolts of cloth and one of purple, chained to the counter. The board says SILK. The cloth disagrees.

info.name: Clothing Stall C
info.text: Tunics with neat holes in them. AIRY, says the board, which is one way to describe a spear wound.

info.name: Clothing Stall D
info.text: A tub of pink water and a washboard. CLEAN, promises the board. The last tunic on the line has its doubts.

info.name: Crops Stall
info.text: Cabbages, turnips, sacks of grain and onion braids. Grown on good soil; the battlefield next door keeps it rich.

info.name: Crops Double Stall N
info.text: Baskets, crates, onion braids and a scale. ALMOST FRESH, which in the arena district counts as a promise.

info.name: Crops Double Stall E
info.text: Baskets, crates, onion braids and a scale. ALMOST FRESH, which in the arena district counts as a promise.

info.name: Crops Double Stall S
info.text: Baskets, crates, onion braids and a scale. ALMOST FRESH, which in the arena district counts as a promise.

info.name: Crops Double Stall W
info.text: Baskets, crates, onion braids and a scale. ALMOST FRESH, which in the arena district counts as a promise.

info.name: Crops Market Tent N
info.text: A big green tent of grain, cabbage and crates. FARM FRESH: the farm is behind the arena, where the sand is dumped.

info.name: Crops Market Tent E
info.text: A big green tent of grain, cabbage and crates. FARM FRESH: the farm is behind the arena, where the sand is dumped.

info.name: Crops Market Tent S
info.text: A big green tent of grain, cabbage and crates. FARM FRESH: the farm is behind the arena, where the sand is dumped.

info.name: Crops Market Tent W
info.text: A big green tent of grain, cabbage and crates. FARM FRESH: the farm is behind the arena, where the sand is dumped.

info.name: Crops Stall B
info.text: Crates of apples, olives and lemons, with herbs drying at the back. CHEAP, says the board, and it tastes like it.

info.name: Crops Stall C
info.text: Grain, onions and a crooked scale with a stone under one pan. FAIR, says the board. To the vendor.

info.name: Crops Stall D
info.text: A mouldy heap in the corner and two baskets of the same. HALF PRICE. Still overpriced.

info.name: Drink Stall
info.text: Sealed amphorae, cups and a jug of the good stuff. The good stuff and the cheap stuff come from the same jug.

info.name: Drink Double Stall N
info.text: Amphorae on one side, barrels on the other, one long bar between. WATERED WINE: at least they are honest.

info.name: Drink Double Stall E
info.text: Amphorae on one side, barrels on the other, one long bar between. WATERED WINE: at least they are honest.

info.name: Drink Double Stall S
info.text: Amphorae on one side, barrels on the other, one long bar between. WATERED WINE: at least they are honest.

info.name: Drink Double Stall W
info.text: Amphorae on one side, barrels on the other, one long bar between. WATERED WINE: at least they are honest.

info.name: Drink Market Tent N
info.text: Barrels, a big jar of water and cups on every table. LAST ROUND, says the board, every round, until somebody dies.

info.name: Drink Market Tent E
info.text: Barrels, a big jar of water and cups on every table. LAST ROUND, says the board, every round, until somebody dies.

info.name: Drink Market Tent S
info.text: Barrels, a big jar of water and cups on every table. LAST ROUND, says the board, every round, until somebody dies.

info.name: Drink Market Tent W
info.text: Barrels, a big jar of water and cups on every table. LAST ROUND, says the board, every round, until somebody dies.

info.name: Drink Stall B
info.text: Barrels, wineskins and a row of cups. BEER, says the board. Gladiators drink it before a fight and wish they had not.

info.name: Drink Stall C
info.text: A big jar of water, a ladle and something floating in it. WATER, says the board. Mostly.

info.name: Drink Stall D
info.text: A barrel on its side, a purple puddle and eleven chalk marks for credit. CASH, says the board now.

info.name: Exotic Food Stall
info.text: A cold grill with skewers of something and cones of spice. YUM?, asks the board. The question is the honest part.

info.name: Exotic Food Double Stall N
info.text: Spices on one side, skewers on the other. ASK NOTHING, says the board, and the regulars never do.

info.name: Exotic Food Double Stall E
info.text: Spices on one side, skewers on the other. ASK NOTHING, says the board, and the regulars never do.

info.name: Exotic Food Double Stall S
info.text: Spices on one side, skewers on the other. ASK NOTHING, says the board, and the regulars never do.

info.name: Exotic Food Double Stall W
info.text: Spices on one side, skewers on the other. ASK NOTHING, says the board, and the regulars never do.

info.name: Exotic Food Market Tent N
info.text: A tent of jars, kettles and coloured cones. NO REFUNDS, and nobody has ever come back to ask for one.

info.name: Exotic Food Market Tent E
info.text: A tent of jars, kettles and coloured cones. NO REFUNDS, and nobody has ever come back to ask for one.

info.name: Exotic Food Market Tent S
info.text: A tent of jars, kettles and coloured cones. NO REFUNDS, and nobody has ever come back to ask for one.

info.name: Exotic Food Market Tent W
info.text: A tent of jars, kettles and coloured cones. NO REFUNDS, and nobody has ever come back to ask for one.

info.name: Exotic Food Stall B
info.text: Dried pods on strings and cones of spice in every colour. SPICY: enough to cover the taste of anything.

info.name: Exotic Food Stall C
info.text: Jars of the unexplained and a pot of black soup. The board just says ????. So does the stomach.

info.name: Exotic Food Stall D
info.text: A big kettle with a bone sticking out. TODAY, says the board, and nobody dares ask what today is.

info.name: Market Stall: Food
info.text: Bread, sausages and a pot of stew that has been simmering since the last games. Nobody asks what is in it.

info.name: Market Stall: Food A
info.text: Cheese wheels, oil jars and a smell that follows you home. Cheaper by the wheel, cheaper still by the funeral.

info.name: Market Stall: Food B
info.text: Honey cakes for the winners, garum for everyone else. The chalk marks are what the gladiators still owe.

info.name: Market Stall: Food C
info.text: Fresh meat, says the board, with a question mark. The bone in the stew is the honest part.

info.name: Market Stall: Household
info.text: Jugs, plates and pots for a home you will rarely see between bouts. Every crack is a feature.

info.name: Market Stall: Household A
info.text: Lamps and candles, unlit for safety and for profit. Darkness is free, light costs extra.

info.name: Market Stall: Household B
info.text: Writing tablets, soap and a stool. Write your will, wash your hands, sit down before the news.

info.name: Market Stall: Household C
info.text: The heap of shards is not for sale. It was already sold, to whoever broke it.

info.name: Market Stall: Intermediate Goods
info.text: Planks, iron bars and rope for people who build things that outlast them. Mostly arenas.

info.name: Market Stall: Materials A
info.text: Bricks, roof tiles and lime. Everything you need for a wall, except a reason to stay behind it.

info.name: Market Stall: Materials B
info.text: Barrels, empty amphorae, nails and tools. Bring your own bent nails back for half a copper.

info.name: Market Stall: Materials C
info.text: Strong rope, pre-knotted for your convenience. The trader swears it is for hanging laundry.

info.name: Market Stall: Luxury
info.text: Gold on a tray, a mirror on a stand and perfume to cover the arena smell. Prices on request, regrets on delivery.

info.name: Market Stall: Luxury A
info.text: Victor's wreaths and gold bars for those who bet correctly. The losers' wreaths are sold at the other stall.

info.name: Market Stall: Luxury B
info.text: Purple cloth, silver plates and a small chest. Dress like a senator, eat like one, owe like one.

info.name: Market Stall: Luxury C
info.text: GUARDED, says the board. The guard stepped out, his spear did not, and the chest lock is already on the ground.

info.name: Market Stall: Raw Materials
info.text: Ore by the basket and by the heap. The pickaxe is not for sale, the stain on it is not discussed.

info.name: Market Stall: Raw Materials A
info.text: Salt, sulphur and natron in open sacks. Preserve food, start fires, embalm the unlucky. One-stop shop.

info.name: Market Stall: Raw Materials B
info.text: Logs, clay and reed bundles. Raw goods for raw people, weighed generously in the seller's favour.

info.name: Market Stall: Raw Materials C
info.text: A marble block, solid as advertised, apart from the crack. The red handprint was the last bargain.

info.name: Market Stall: Souvenirs
info.text: Bloodied rags on a line, bone dice and bottled sweat of champions. Sweat may be from the trader.

info.name: Market Stall: Souvenirs A
info.text: Little clay helmets in rows, one for every gladiator who ever lost. The shelf keeps getting longer.

info.name: Market Stall: Souvenirs B
info.text: Wooden swords and tridents for children who want to die young like their heroes. Lamps sold separately.

info.name: Market Stall: Souvenirs C
info.text: A jar of teeth, labelled REAL. For once the board is not lying.

info.name: Market Stall: Vice
info.text: Creeper leaves upside down, gorgon dust in bowls and flasks of something clear. The chalk tally is the stall's real ledger.

info.name: Market Stall: Vice A
info.text: Baskets of bacchant berries and bacchant's tears. Sweet on the tongue, sour on the purse, gone by morning.

info.name: Market Stall: Vice B
info.text: Hydra reeds in bundles and a row of pipes. Breathe deep, cough later, pay now.

info.name: Market Stall: Vice C
info.text: A barrel of Lethe water with a ladle on a chain. FORGET, says the board, including the price.

info.name: Wall Walk
info.text: Wide enough for two soldiers, or one soldier and his excuses.

info.name: Wall Crown Half W
info.text: Half a wall, so the city looks round. The other half was never paid for.

info.name: Wall Crown Half N
info.text: Half a wall, so the city looks round. The other half was never paid for.

info.name: Wall Crown Half E
info.text: Half a wall, so the city looks round. The other half was never paid for.

info.name: Wall Crown Half S
info.text: Half a wall, so the city looks round. The other half was never paid for.

info.name: Slanted Wall
info.text: The wall turns a corner here. Attackers do too, mostly into the moat.

info.name: Slanted Wall A
info.text: A crack the size of a bribe. The mason swears it is decorative.

info.name: Slanted Wall B
info.text: The new stone is where someone was thrown through the old one.

info.name: Slanted Wall C
info.text: Same stones, different order. The masons got paid by the layer.

info.name: Slanted Wall D
info.text: Built in a hurry the year the barbarians were rumoured. They never came. The wall stayed crooked.

info.name: Slanted Battlements W
info.text: Battlements seen edge-on. Thicker than the city budget, at least.

info.name: Slanted Battlements
info.text: Battlements on a bend, for archers who like a view of the whole crowd.

info.name: Slanted Battlements A
info.text: One merlon gave up. So did the guard behind it.

info.name: Slanted Battlements B
info.text: The arrow is a souvenir. The stain is the previous owner of the souvenir.

info.name: Slanted Battlements E
info.text: Battlements seen edge-on. Thicker than the city budget, at least.

info.name: Slanted Battlements Back
info.text: The back of the battlements. Nobody looks at it except the guards, who look at nothing.

info.name: Town Wall
info.text: Built to keep the barbarians out. Mostly keeps the taxpayers in.

info.name: Town Wall
info.text: Every stone paid for twice: once by the city, once more into the mayor's villa.

info.name: Wall Ramp
info.text: Built gentle, so the guards can drag the wounded up and the dead down without tripping. Usually it is the other way round.

info.name: Wall Ramp
info.text: Built gentle, so the guards can drag the wounded up and the dead down without tripping. Usually it is the other way round.

info.name: Battlements
info.text: The gaps are for arrows. The rest is for hiding when the arrows come back.

info.name: Wall Crown N Flat 3/4
info.text: Most of a wall. The rest went into the magistrate's summer villa.

info.name: Wall Crown N Flat 1/4
info.text: A sliver of wall so the city looks round from the sky. The gods were not impressed. The tax collectors were.

info.name: Slanted Wall N Flat 3/4
info.text: The wall bends here, slowly, like a senator changing sides.

info.name: Slanted Wall N Flat 3/4 A
info.text: A crack the mason calls character. The city engineer calls it his retirement plan.

info.text: Battlements on a gentle bend. Archers call it the scenic route; so do the arrows.

info.name: Battlements N Flat 3/4 A
info.text: One merlon gave up. So did the guard behind it.

info.name: Battlements N Flat 3/4 B
info.text: The arrow is a souvenir. The stain is the previous owner of the souvenir.

info.name: Medicus
info.text: A small house with a slate roof and the staff of Asclepius over the door. The medicus sews, sets and saws for gold; the cheaper the treatment, the longer the scream.

info.name: Menagerie
info.text: Pens with a moat and a rail. The rail is for the visitors. The moat is for the lawyers.

info.name: Ore Heap
info.text: Broken rock with a rust-red streak of profit. The shovel is shared; so are the blisters.

info.name: Ore Heap Spilled
info.text: A basket burst and the ore went everywhere. The basket will be docked from somebody's wages.

info.name: Ore Baskets
info.text: Baskets of ore and a carrying yoke. Mules cost money, so the yoke fits a human neck.

info.name: Pit Props
info.text: Timber to hold the mountain up. It holds most days. The other days are why there is so much timber.

info.name: Sorting Bench
info.text: Ore on the left, waste on the right, thumbs somewhere in between. The roof keeps the rain off the ore.

info.name: Tree Stump
info.text: What is left of a tree after the woodcutter has been by. Give it a few days and it will try again; trees never learn.

info.name: Old Stump
info.text: Grey, mossy and sprouting mushrooms. It has outlasted two foremen and one forest.

info.name: Fresh Stump
info.text: Freshly felled. The chips are still pale and the tree has not yet noticed it is furniture.

info.name: Torn Stump
info.text: The trunk split upwards and kicked back. The woodcutters call it the barber's chair. Nobody sits in it twice.

info.name: Olive Mill N
info.text: Extra virgin, says the jar. The open sack of sand beside it says nothing at all.

info.name: Olive Mill W
info.text: Oil settles in the tanks, coins settle in the locked chest, chalk marks settle the arguments.

info.name: Olive Mill
info.text: Two stones crush olives in a stone bowl. The donkey quit; its yoke waits for a volunteer.

info.name: Olive Mill E
info.text: The red on the millstone is not from olives. The miller now counts his fingers every morning.

info.name: Granary
info.text: A grain store on mushroom stones, because rats cannot climb. The tally says the rats are winning anyway.

info.name: Granary A
info.text: One stone is gone and an amphora holds the corner up. The rats have sent their thanks.

info.name: Granary B
info.text: Sacks under the eaves and a jar marked with a red cross. The red cross is not for the rats.

info.name: Lighthouse
info.text: A stone tower with a fire on top. Ships that see it in time pay the harbour fee. The others pay the wreckers.

info.name: Lighthouse A
info.text: Fire off. The keeper says it saves wood. The wreckers say he has a new business partner.

info.name: Lighthouse B
info.text: A round tower streaked white by gulls. The scratches by the door count ships, not days.

info.name: Smelter Stacks
info.text: Two black stacks over a stone smelter. The slag heap grows faster than the town.

info.name: Smelter Stacks A
info.text: One stack fell in. The other two are said to be perfectly safe, by the man who sold them.

info.name: Smelter Stacks B
info.text: A single tall stack and two slag heaps. NO REST is painted on the board, as a promise.

info.name: Olive Grove
info.text: Gnarled olive trees in rows behind a dry wall. Older than the owners, and kinder too.

info.name: Olive Grove A
info.text: One tree was felled for debt, one leans on a crutch. The grove has the same lender as the town.

info.name: Olive Grove B
info.text: Oil jars waiting for the tax man. The broken one was an accident, the stain was not.

info.name: Olive Grove C
info.text: A ladder with a missing rung and a fresh mound under the tree. The harvest was excellent this year.

info.name: Palace
info.text: Marble, columns, a golden statue taller than the door. The ruler lives here. The town only pays for it.

info.name: Palace A
info.text: The statue lost its head in the last riot. A new one is on order, slightly larger.

info.name: Palace B
info.text: The garden is going wild and the fountain runs red on feast days. Nobody asks what with.

info.name: Pastures
info.text: Fenced grazing with a trough, a hay rack and a bell. The tally board says forty out, thirty-nine back.

info.name: Pastures A
info.text: A broken rail, some bones and a tuft of wool. The fence was technically working.

info.name: Pastures B
info.text: A thatched lean-to for bad weather. The herd stands in the rain anyway; the herder sleeps under it.

info.name: Pastures C
info.text: Shearing day leftovers and a ram skull on the gatepost. The skull is the herd boss now.

info.name: Ruins
info.text: Burnt walls of a quarter that shrank. The tax notice on the door frame survived the fire.

info.name: Ruins A
info.text: Half a house and a sign saying FOR RENT. The landlord is optimistic.

info.name: Ruins B
info.text: Fallen columns, charred beams and weeds. Somebody lived well here, until somebody else came.

info.name: Ruins C
info.text: A tall broken wall and little else. History is written by the winners; the rest is rubble.

info.name: Shipyard
info.text: A half-planked hull on the slipway, ribs bare like a feast after the guests. The tally board counts launches and floats separately.

info.name: Shipyard A
info.text: Keel and ribs only, the skeleton of a ship. Optimists call it a frame, sailors call it a coffin with gaps.

info.name: Shipyard B
info.text: Nearly finished, with a red stripe and a patched plank. The name is painted where the patch will not show.

info.name: Shipyard C
info.text: Burnt to the ribs a week before launch. The owner was insured. The owner is also very relaxed.

info.name: Slum Quarter
info.text: Plank shacks, mud lanes and laundry drying on the roofs. The rent is cheap, the rats pay none.

info.name: Slum Quarter A
info.text: Another tangle of shacks and sacking. The crate with the sign is for let. It has a view of the other crate.

info.name: Slum Quarter B
info.text: Thatch on one shack, a barrel on the lane. Locals call this end of the quarter the posh end.

info.name: Slum Quarter C
info.text: Boards over the big puddle, gaps in every wall. The puddle has lived here longer than anyone.

info.name: Slum Quarter D
info.text: One shack burnt down last night. The sign says fire sale. Everything left is ash, and the ash is negotiable.

info.name: Suburbs
info.text: Whitewashed cottages with gardens outside the walls. Cheaper rent, fresher air, free bandits on weekends.

info.name: Suburbs A
info.text: A thatched cottage next to a tiled one. The neighbours have not spoken since the roof went up.

info.name: Suburbs B
info.text: Turnips, an amphora and a trough. The red cross on the door means the tax man has already been. Twice.

info.name: Suburbs C
info.text: One cottage stands empty, door boarded and scorched. The note says they moved inside the walls. Nobody believes the note.

info.name: Theatre
info.text: A half bowl of stone seats facing a wooden stage. The trapdoor is for dramatic exits; some actors take it more literally.

info.name: Theatre A
info.text: Broken seats patched with planks. Splinters come free with every ticket, applause costs extra.

info.name: Theatre B
info.text: Half the upper rows fell in during a comedy. Critics agree it brought the house down.

info.name: Vineyards
info.text: Terraced vines, stone walls and a pressing basin stained for good. The skull on the stake keeps crows away and pickers honest.

info.name: Vineyards A
info.text: Harvest is over. Bare canes, empty rows, and a vintner counting baskets twice.

info.name: Vineyards B
info.text: Heavy grapes and full baskets. A good year, said everyone who did not carry them.

info.name: Vineyards C
info.text: Autumn leaves and a cracked amphora. The wine inside was already vinegar; the jar had good taste.

info.name: Vineyards D
info.text: Trampled vines, red mud and one lost boot. Either a very wild harvest festival or a fight about the borders.

info.name: Watermill
info.text: A stone mill on a fast stream. It grinds grain, bark and anything that falls in. The miller swears it is mostly grain.

info.name: Watermill A
info.text: Moss on the wheel, two paddles missing. It still turns, slower than the debts.

info.name: Watermill B
info.text: Whitewashed, tiled and proud. Same stream, same flour, higher prices.

info.name: Watermill C
info.text: Something came down the stream and stopped at the wheel. The flour tastes of nothing unusual. Officially.

info.name: Pen Gate N
info.text: A gate of split wood with an iron ring. Close it behind you, or chase the goats yourself.

info.name: Pen Gate E
info.text: A gate of split wood with an iron ring. Close it behind you, or chase the goats yourself.

info.name: Pen Gate S
info.text: A gate of split wood with an iron ring. Close it behind you, or chase the goats yourself.

info.name: Pen Gate W
info.text: A gate of split wood with an iron ring. Close it behind you, or chase the goats yourself.

info.name: Pen Fence N
info.text: Two rails and a post. It keeps the goats in and the neighbours honest.

info.name: Pen Fence Patched N
info.text: A leaning post tied up with rope. Holds until somebody leans on it.

info.name: Pen Fence Broken N
info.text: A broken rail tied with a red rag, a bone hung on the post. Wolves are expected to read the hint.

info.name: Pen Fence E
info.text: Two rails and a post. It keeps the goats in and the neighbours honest.

info.name: Pen Fence Patched E
info.text: A leaning post tied up with rope. Holds until somebody leans on it.

info.name: Pen Fence Broken E
info.text: A broken rail tied with a red rag, a bone hung on the post. Wolves are expected to read the hint.

info.name: Pen Fence S
info.text: Two rails and a post. It keeps the goats in and the neighbours honest.

info.name: Pen Fence Patched S
info.text: A leaning post tied up with rope. Holds until somebody leans on it.

info.name: Pen Fence Broken S
info.text: A broken rail tied with a red rag, a bone hung on the post. Wolves are expected to read the hint.

info.name: Pen Fence W
info.text: Two rails and a post. It keeps the goats in and the neighbours honest.

info.name: Pen Fence Patched W
info.text: A leaning post tied up with rope. Holds until somebody leans on it.

info.name: Pen Fence Broken W
info.text: A broken rail tied with a red rag, a bone hung on the post. Wolves are expected to read the hint.

info.name: Basalt Paving
info.text: Big black stones laid by slaves who were not allowed to walk on them afterwards. The road outlived every one of them.

info.name: Basalt Paving (ruts)
info.text: Two grooves worn by a thousand carts. The wheels know the way to the arena better than the drivers.

info.name: Basalt Paving (ruts)
info.text: Two grooves worn by a thousand carts. Step into one at night and you will limp to your own funeral.

info.name: Basalt Paving (dung)
info.text: A mule passed here recently. The street sweepers pass less often.

info.name: Basalt Paving (pothole)
info.text: A stone was pried loose and sold. The puddle is free of charge.

info.name: Basalt Paving (sandal)
info.text: One sandal, one dried stain. The other sandal left in a hurry.

info.name: Basalt Paving
info.text: Basalt from the quarry. Rumour says the quarry still wants its workers back.

info.name: Basalt Paving
info.text: Polished by bare feet, chariot wheels and the occasional dragged body.

info.name: Cobbled Alley
info.text: Round stones packed into dirt. Good for twisting ankles and hiding small coins.

info.name: Cobbled Alley (rubbish)
info.text: Shards, a cabbage leaf, a bone. Nobody asks whose bone.

info.name: Cobbled Alley (puddle)
info.text: A puddle that never dries. Do not ask what it is made of.

info.name: Cobbled Alley (gap)
info.text: The stones ran out before the alley did. A weed took over the job.

info.name: Cobbled Alley (rat)
info.text: A dead rat, feet up. The neighbourhood held a small, hungry vigil.

info.name: Cobbled Alley
info.text: Cobbles worn smooth by people who could not afford a litter.

info.name: Cobbled Alley
info.text: Every stone wobbles a little. So does everyone who walks here after dark.

info.name: Forum Marble
info.text: Marble slabs where senators walk. Everyone else walks around them.

info.name: Forum Marble (mended)
info.text: A crack sealed with cheap filler. Like the republic.

info.name: Forum Marble (inscription)
info.text: A donor's name, half chiselled off after his trial. The rest of him was removed elsewhere.

info.name: Forum Marble (pigeons)
info.text: Pigeons have their own opinion of the senate and express it daily.

info.name: Forum Marble
info.text: Veined marble from far away, paid for by people who will never stand on it.

info.name: Market Flagstones
info.text: Square slabs for square deals. The deals are rarely square.

info.name: Market Flagstones (crack)
info.text: Cracked under a fishmonger's cart. The fishmonger was fined; the slab was not fixed.

info.name: Market Flagstones (chalk)
info.text: Children chalked a hopping game. Their parents chalked prices next to it.

info.name: Market Flagstones (scraps)
info.text: Rotten fruit and cabbage. Breakfast for beggars, ammunition for the arena crowd.

info.name: Market Flagstones
info.text: Flagstones scrubbed once a year, for the festival of the god of hygiene, who is not popular.

info.name: Outpost Hut 2 1 N
info.text: A stone hut under rotting thatch. Twelve men sleep in shifts, so nobody ever has to see the inside awake.

info.name: Outpost Hut 2 1 E
info.text: A stone hut under rotting thatch. Twelve men sleep in shifts, so nobody ever has to see the inside awake.

info.name: Outpost Hut 2 1 S
info.text: A stone hut under rotting thatch. Twelve men sleep in shifts, so nobody ever has to see the inside awake.

info.name: Outpost Hut 2 1 W
info.text: A stone hut under rotting thatch. Twelve men sleep in shifts, so nobody ever has to see the inside awake.

info.name: Outpost Hut 2 2 N
info.text: The roof is patched with planks, the door with a pay notice. The red cross means paid in full, or paid for in full.

info.name: Outpost Hut 2 2 E
info.text: The roof is patched with planks, the door with a pay notice. The red cross means paid in full, or paid for in full.

info.name: Rival Ludus A
info.text: A rival school with its own yard, posts and banners. Its graduates are buried neatly by the wall.

info.name: Rival Ludus B
info.text: Purple banners, polished wooden swords, one missing. The rival calls it discipline; the graves call it tuition.

info.name: Rival Ludus C
info.text: Green banners and fewer posts. They train less and bury more, which saves on wooden swords.

info.name: Rival Ludus D
info.text: The gate is smashed and the sand is fresh red. Rival schools settle disputes the traditional way.

info.name: Saltworks A
info.text: Shallow pans, a cold boiling pan and white heaps. Salt keeps fish, meat and grudges fresh for years.

info.name: Saltworks B
info.text: A big new heap and full baskets. The overseer weighs the salt twice and the wages once.

info.name: Saltworks C
info.text: The boiling pan cracked, the crack is filed under next year. The workers boil on regardless.

info.name: Saltworks D
info.text: A boot sticks out of the big heap and a shovel stands beside it. Nobody has asked, which is very well preserved.

info.name: Smugglers' Cove A
info.text: A cave, a boat and barrels with the seals scraped off. The sign says fishing only; the fish pay no duty either.

info.name: Smugglers' Cove B
info.text: The boat lies keel up, the barrels moved deeper in. The tide is the only thing here that gets inspected.

info.name: Smugglers' Cove C
info.text: Firewood in red and white stripes. Somewhere a toll barrier is missing and nobody here has seen it.

info.name: Smugglers' Cove D
info.text: The last customs inspector stayed. His bronze badge is still shiny, the rest of him less so.

info.name: Mine Adit 1 N
info.text: The tally board counts men going in and men coming out. The two rows have never once agreed.

info.name: Mine Adit 1 E
info.text: The tally board counts men going in and men coming out. The two rows have never once agreed.

info.name: Mine Adit 1 S
info.text: The tally board counts men going in and men coming out. The two rows have never once agreed.

info.name: Mine Adit 1 W
info.text: The tally board counts men going in and men coming out. The two rows have never once agreed.

info.name: Mine Adit 2 N
info.text: The cap beam cracked last month. It is now held up by a rope, a crooked prop and the foreman's optimism.

info.name: Mine Adit 2 E
info.text: The cap beam cracked last month. It is now held up by a rope, a crooked prop and the foreman's optimism.

info.name: Mine Adit 2 S
info.text: The cap beam cracked last month. It is now held up by a rope, a crooked prop and the foreman's optimism.

info.name: Mine Adit 2 W
info.text: The cap beam cracked last month. It is now held up by a rope, a crooked prop and the foreman's optimism.

info.name: Toll Station A
info.text: A barrier, a toll hut and the lord's shield on the wall. The fee is fixed; the man collecting it is not.

info.name: Toll Station B
info.text: Barrier up, tally on the wall. Somebody paid, or somebody important pretended to.

info.name: Toll Station C
info.text: The barrier broke and is tied with rope, the old one is firewood. Taxes, at least, never break.

info.name: Toll Station D
info.text: An empty iron cage hangs by the hut. It is not for sale, but it is for rent.

info.name: Trading Post A
info.text: A shed, a scale and two stalls at the crossroads. The scale is honest; the little bronze lump on the beam is not.

info.name: Trading Post B
info.text: Plank roof, ripe fruit, fresh prices in chalk. The prices ripen faster than the fruit.

info.name: Trading Post C
info.text: One awning collapsed, the fruit went under a cart. The trader sells the bruised ones as local.

info.name: Trading Post D
info.text: Chains on the counter, collars on the posts. Everything has a price here, sooner or later everyone.

info.name: Hut Gear Bruch 2 E
info.text: A sledgehammer, chisels on a stone bench, a basket of iron wedges. The stone is patient; the masons are paid by the block.

info.name: Hut Gear Bruch 2 S
info.text: A sledgehammer, chisels on a stone bench, a basket of iron wedges. The stone is patient; the masons are paid by the block.

info.name: Hut Gear Bruch 3 E
info.text: A sledgehammer, chisels on a stone bench, a basket of iron wedges. The stone is patient; the masons are paid by the block.

info.name: Hut Gear Bruch 3 S
info.text: A sledgehammer, chisels on a stone bench, a basket of iron wedges. The stone is patient; the masons are paid by the block.

info.name: Hut Gear Fischer 2 N
info.text: A net drying on the wall, two oars and a wicker fish trap. The trap catches fish; the net catches the fisherman's debts.

info.name: Hut Gear Fischer 2 E
info.text: A net drying on the wall, two oars and a wicker fish trap. The trap catches fish; the net catches the fisherman's debts.

info.name: Hut Gear Fischer 2 S
info.text: A net drying on the wall, two oars and a wicker fish trap. The trap catches fish; the net catches the fisherman's debts.

info.name: Hut Gear Fischer 3 N
info.text: A net drying on the wall, two oars and a wicker fish trap. The trap catches fish; the net catches the fisherman's debts.

info.name: Hut Gear Fischer 3 W
info.text: A net drying on the wall, two oars and a wicker fish trap. The trap catches fish; the net catches the fisherman's debts.

info.name: Hut Gear Holz 2 E
info.text: Two axes, a crosscut saw and a bundle of kindling. The saw needs two men, which is why there are always two men.

info.name: Hut Gear Holz 2 S
info.text: Two axes, a crosscut saw and a bundle of kindling. The saw needs two men, which is why there are always two men.

info.name: Hut Gear Holz 3 E

info.name: Hut Gear Holz 3 W
info.text: Two axes, a crosscut saw and a bundle of kindling. The saw needs two men, which is why there are always two men.

info.name: Hut Gear Jagd 2 E
info.text: Spears, a bow, snares on a nail and a hide pegged to the wall. The hunter is the only man here who is paid by the corpse.

info.name: Hut Gear Jagd 2 S
info.text: Spears, a bow, snares on a nail and a hide pegged to the wall. The hunter is the only man here who is paid by the corpse.

info.name: Queue Path
info.text: Packed gravel between worn boards. Waiting is half the fun.

info.name: Queue Path A
info.text: Footprints, all facing forward. Nobody turns back once they have paid.

info.name: Queue Path B
info.text: A dropped entry token. Someone will be very upset at the gate.

info.name: Queue Path C
info.text: A tooth and a stain. The queue got impatient.

info.name: Queue Path Across
info.text: The same patient gravel, turned the other way. Queues bend, hope does not.

info.name: Queue Path Across A
info.text: Footprints the other way round. Still nobody turning back.

info.name: Vine Row
info.text: Vines trained on posts and wire, heavy with dark grapes. The grapes are crushed by feet, the workers by the vintner.

info.name: Vine Row B
info.text: Leaves turning yellow, grapes ripe. Harvest is near, and so are the thieves.

info.name: Vine Row (broken post)
info.text: A post gave way and the basket went with it. The grapes are now stomped for free.

info.name: Vine Row J
info.text: Vines trained on posts and wire, heavy with dark grapes. The grapes are crushed by feet, the workers by the vintner.

info.name: Vine Row B J
info.text: Leaves turning yellow, grapes ripe. Harvest is near, and so are the thieves.

info.name: Vine Row (broken post) J
info.text: A post gave way and the basket went with it. The grapes are now stomped for free.

info.name: Raked Salt Pond
info.text: Salt raked into a heap in the corner, the rake left on the wall. The overseer has already weighed it with his eyes.

info.name: Salt Crust Pond
info.text: The water has gone and left a white crust. Walk on it barefoot once and you will know why the workers walk on the walls.

info.name: Brine Pond
info.text: Sea water in a mud-walled pond, waiting for the sun. The sun works for free and is still the most reliable worker.

info.name: Salt Heap
info.text: A white cone of salt with rake marks around it. Rain is the only thief the guards cannot flog.

info.name: Salt Baskets
info.text: Baskets of salt, tied sacks and a tally stick. Soldiers are paid in this stuff; the soldiers would like a word.

info.name: Boiling Pan
info.text: A lead pan on a stone hearth, crusted white. Boil the brine, scrape the salt, cough the lead. Two of three are paid.

info.name: Closed Sign
info.text: A plank on a stick: CLOSED. The crowd reads it, sighs, and goes into town to watch a hanging instead.

info.name: Senate Banner Blank
info.text: A faction banner: two old banners sewn together by a coalition that agreed on nothing but the needle. Somebody has already voted with a knife.

info.name: Senate Banner Blank I
info.text: A faction banner: two old banners sewn together by a coalition that agreed on nothing but the needle. Somebody has already voted with a knife.

info.name: Senate N
info.text: Behind the senate lie the ballots of the last vote, all of them. The result was announced before they were counted.

info.name: Senate W
info.text: The stain on the steps is old. They scrubbed it once, for the ceremony, then voted that it was not there.

info.name: Senate
info.text: The senate: fake marble over honest brick. Two letters of SENATVS were stolen in bronze; nobody has voted to replace them.

info.name: Senate E
info.text: A seat is for sale, a senator sleeps on the steps, and the donations chest by the door is the only thing here that works.

info.name: Slave Market
info.text: A stage, a block and a pen. Prices on the board, chains on the posts, smiles on the trader.

info.name: Extra Stands
info.text: Four rows of splinters with a view. Cushions sold separately, splinters free.

info.name: Governor Banner Blank
info.text: An empty banner. The last coat of arms was cut off with the last governor's head; the new one has not paid the embroiderer yet.

info.name: Governor Banner Blank I
info.text: An empty banner. The last coat of arms was cut off with the last governor's head; the new one has not paid the embroiderer yet.

info.name: Governor's Palace N
info.text: The back of the governor's palace. Tax files spill from the windows; nobody has ever read one, everybody has paid one.

info.name: Governor's Palace W
info.text: Where the province is governed: slowly, expensively, and with a good view of the fish pond.

info.name: Governor's Palace
info.text: Columns out front, heads on spikes above, a pillory below. The governor rules from the courtyard, reclining.

info.name: Governor's Palace E
info.text: A courtyard with morays, a peacock and chained tax chests. Complaints go in the box by the door, where spiders file them.

info.name: Wooden Jetty
info.text: Planks on stilts above the water. Each board has been walked on by a sailor, a fishwife and at least one fool who jumped.

info.name: Wooden Jetty
info.text: Planks on stilts above the water. The gaps are wide enough for a coin and exactly wide enough for a ring.

info.name: Jetty Ramp
info.text: One step up from the quay. Drunks take it in one stride, the tax collector in three.

info.name: Jetty Ramp
info.text: One step up from the quay. Drunks take it in one stride, the tax collector in three.

info.text: The School of Polite Doubt. Not a religion, it insists, while collecting the offerings.

info.name: Great Temple Rear
info.text: The back of a great temple. Even the gods need somewhere to keep the firewood.

info.name: Great Temple Rear I
info.text: The back of a great temple. The pigeons have formed their own priesthood here.

info.name: Great Temple
info.text: Columns all round, a horned altar and a pyre out front. Big city, big gods, bigger collection box.

info.name: Great Temple I
info.text: Twenty-two columns, one altar, one pyre. The priests insist the smell is incense.

info.name: Small Temple Rear
info.text: The back of a small temple. The pigeons consider it theirs, and the gods have not objected.

info.name: Small Temple Rear I
info.text: The back of a small temple, where the priests leave by the side door with the takings.

info.name: Small Temple
info.text: Marble, columns and a blood altar out front. The gods are said to listen; the priests certainly count.

info.name: Small Temple I
info.text: Marble, columns and a blood altar out front. Donations are voluntary and strictly enforced.

info.name: Theatre N
info.text: Seen from the cheap seats: arches, masts and a sail that gave up. The stage blood is real; the actor is on sick leave.

info.name: Theatre W
info.text: Proper seats for the rich, cushions for the richer, splinters for everyone else. The masks have seen worse.

info.name: Theatre
info.text: Eleven rows of stone, one stage and a sail with more holes than plot. Tonight: a tragedy, performed with real knives for authenticity.

info.name: Theatre E
info.text: The gate leads to culture, the arches to the latrines. Rotten fruit is sold at the door, for critics.

info.name: Roe Deer
info.text: A roe deer, all eyes and nerves. It grazes, it listens, and it has no idea there is a kitchen in its future.

info.name: Gate Arch
info.text: The wall walk crosses here. Guards spit on whoever passes underneath, as tradition demands.

info.name: Gate Arch

info.name: Heads on Spikes I
info.text: The gate keeps a guest list. Current entries no longer object to the view.

info.name: Heads on Spikes I A
info.text: The crow has a standing reservation.

info.name: Heads on Spikes J
info.text: The gate keeps a guest list. Current entries no longer object to the view.

info.name: Heads on Spikes J A
info.text: The crow has a standing reservation.

info.name: Training Yard
info.text: Sand, posts and wooden swords. The posts always win the first year.

info.name: Tower Guard Door
info.text: Where the garrison storms out when the bell rings and staggers in when the wine runs out. The tally above the door is not for victories.

info.name: Tower Guard Door
info.text: Where the garrison storms out when the bell rings and staggers in when the wine runs out. The tally above the door is not for victories.

info.name: Wall Tower
info.text: Three floors of stairs so a guard can look at nothing from a little higher up.

info.name: Wall Tower
info.text: Three floors of stairs so a guard can look at nothing from a little higher up.

info.name: Arrow Slit
info.text: Narrow enough to stop an arrow, wide enough to drop the night soil on visitors.

info.name: Arrow Slit
info.text: Narrow enough to stop an arrow, wide enough to drop the night soil on visitors.

info.name: Tower Door
info.text: Opens onto the wall walk. Locked from the inside whenever the enemy is outside, and sometimes when he is not.

info.name: Tower Door
info.text: Opens onto the wall walk. Locked from the inside whenever the enemy is outside, and sometimes when he is not.

info.name: Reed Stooks
info.text: Reed sheaves stood up to dry. In a month they will be a roof; in ten years they will be the reason the roof leaks.

info.name: Reed Bundles
info.text: Bundles of cut reed, tied twice and stacked. The cutters stand knee-deep for this, and the leeches are not on the payroll.

info.name: Peat Stacks
info.text: Peat turves stacked loosely to dry. Wet peat weighs a ton and burns like an apology; dry peat is worth the wait.

info.name: Peat Barrow
info.text: A barrow full of turves and a basket for the rest. The bog once gave back a whole man. He was still owed wages.

info.name: Stone Wall
info.text: A wall of cut stone with moss at its foot. Keeps the weather out and the workforce in.

info.name: Gate
info.text: A double gate with bronze bands, wide enough for an ox cart. It opens for deliveries and closes for second thoughts.

info.name: Door
info.text: A plank door with a bronze handle, wide enough for one man. Carts, oxen and big ideas have to use the gate.

info.name: Planks
info.text: A neat stack of sawn planks. Today a workshop wall, tomorrow perhaps a lid.

info.name: Meat
info.text: A fresh haunch on a board. Best not to ask which animal, as long as it was an animal.

info.name: Flour
info.text: Two sacks of flour, one with a gnawed hole. The rat is fed; the gladiators are next.

info.name: Flour B
info.text: An open sack with the scoop still in it. Someone left in a hurry, and only one sandal.

info.name: Flour C
info.text: Three sacks and a red handprint. The miller argued about the weight and lost.

info.name: Gold Bars
info.text: A neat stack of bars on a pallet. The top one is bitten: the tax collector checks everything personally.

info.name: Gold Bars B
info.text: An iron-bound crate of gold with a chain and lock. Guarded day and night by whoever is cheapest.

info.name: Gold Bars C
info.text: Loose bars, a chain, a padlock and a little blood. The previous owner signed with his whole hand.

info.name: Hay
info.text: A tied bale of hay with a lost sandal strap. Somebody slept here and did not wake up rested.

info.name: Hay B
info.text: A loose heap with a pitchfork stuck in it. The red on the tines is rust. Mostly.

info.name: Hay C
info.text: Two bales, and a sword hilt poking out. Never look for a needle in the arena's haystack.

info.name: Hides
info.text: Three raw hides with the ludus brand. Tagged, counted and no longer attached to anyone.

info.name: Hides B
info.text: A hide stretched on a lacing frame, scraper waiting below. Patience, salt and a strong stomach.

info.name: Hides C
info.text: Rolled hides tied with twine. They roll better than the previous owners ever did.

info.name: Honey
info.text: Sealed pots of honey, dripping. Sweet enough to make any arena ration go down.

info.name: Honey B
info.text: A straw skep and a full pot. The bees are out on strike, which is why the beekeeper is still alive.

info.name: Honey C
info.text: A cracked pot bleeding honey, dipper in hand. Sticky floors slow down fleeing slaves nicely.

info.name: Horses
info.text: Saddle and bridle on a trestle, plus one spare horseshoe. The rest of the horse went to the sausage stand.

info.name: Horses B
info.text: Saddle, coiled reins, whip and horseshoes. Everything a charioteer needs except a reason to live.

info.name: Horses C
info.text: A padded collar and horseshoes on a post. Mounts sold separately, return policy: none.

info.name: Leather
info.text: Tanned sheets strapped in a stack, sandals on top. One size fits whoever survives.

info.name: Leather B
info.text: Rolls of leather with a blank price tag. Price on request, origin best not requested.

info.name: Leather C
info.text: A sheet draped over a trestle with the tanner's knife still in the beam. He went for lunch. Probably.

info.name: Marble
info.text: A block of quarry marble with chalk tally marks. Each mark is a quarry worker it fell on.

info.name: Marble B
info.text: Stacked slabs and the foot of a victor's statue. The rest was melted down after his last fight.

info.name: Marble C
info.text: A cracked block with hammer, chisel and a red smear. Quarry accidents are included in the price.

info.name: Meal
info.text: A tub of barracks gruel, thick enough that the spoon stands up. So do the complaints.

info.name: Meal B
info.text: Three bowls of gruel, one tipped over. Somebody found a tooth in it and it was not his.

info.name: Meal C
info.text: A cauldron of gruel with a bone sticking out. Mutton, the cook swears. On his mother's grave, which he dug himself.

info.name: Mutton
info.text: A leg of mutton on the chopping block, cleaver in place. Definitely sheep. The cook checked twice.

info.name: Mutton B
info.text: Two legs on a board with a note saying fresh. The note is from three days ago.

info.name: Mutton C
info.text: Legs of mutton hanging from hooks and dripping. The rack is borrowed from the punishment yard.

info.name: Oats
info.text: An open sack of oats and a spill. Horse food, gladiator food, depending on the budget.

info.name: Oats B
info.text: A wicker basket of oats with a sack behind. Porridge for the brave, porridge for the dead.

info.name: Oats C
info.text: Two tied sacks and a fresh sheaf. Harvested by hand, threshed by whoever lost the bet.

info.name: Olive Oil
info.text: Two amphorae of oil, one seeping. Rubbed on fighters, lamps and the floor where the losers slip.

info.name: Olive Oil B
info.text: A tall amphora on a stand, leaking. The puddle is premium grade and very slippery.

info.name: Olive Oil C
info.text: Jugs and a tipped flask. Spilled oil is a tragedy; spilled gladiator is a Tuesday.

info.name: Logs
info.text: Three trimmed logs, stacked. Heavy, splintery and always needed somewhere uphill.

info.name: Water
info.text: A bucket of river water, clear enough if you ignore the rat. The rat stopped complaining days ago.

info.name: Gold Sluice
info.text: A sloping trough with riffles that catch the heavy grains. Gold sinks, sand runs off, hope does both.

info.name: Washed Gravel
info.text: Washed gravel, stacked pans and a chest chained to a stake. The chain is for the gold, the stake is for the washers.

info.name: Corduroy Road
info.text: Logs laid across the mud so the forest swallows travellers more slowly.

info.name: Corduroy Road (Missing Log)
info.text: One log is missing. Something in the hole has been chewing on whatever fell in.

info.name: Corduroy Road (Rotten Logs)
info.text: Two logs have rotted soft. The moss is holding the road together now.

info.name: Corduroy Road (Tally Marks)
info.text: Someone carved tally marks into a log. Either days on the road or days until payment.

info.name: Corduroy Road (Red Rag)
info.text: A red rag tied to a log marks the spot. Nobody remembers what happened there; everybody walks faster.

info.name: Corduroy Road NE
info.text: Logs laid across the mud so the forest swallows travellers more slowly. Runs north-east.

info.name: Corduroy Road (Missing Log) NE
info.text: One log is missing. Something in the hole has been chewing on whatever fell in. Runs north-east.

info.name: Corduroy Road (Rotten Logs) NE
info.text: Two logs have rotted soft. The moss is holding the road together now. Runs north-east.

info.name: Corduroy Road (Tally Marks) NE
info.text: Someone carved tally marks into a log. Either days on the road or days until payment. Runs north-east.

info.name: Corduroy Road (Red Rag) NE
info.text: A red rag tied to a log marks the spot. Nobody remembers what happened there; everybody walks faster. Runs north-east.

info.name: Ferry
info.text: A raft on a rope across the river. The ferryman pulls; the passengers pay; the river decides.

info.name: Ferry (Rope)
info.text: The ferry rope across open water. Hold on to it if the raft is elsewhere.

info.name: Ferry (Old Rope)
info.text: The ferry rope across open water. It is older than the ferryman and in better shape.

info.name: Ferry (Rag and Barrel)
info.text: A red rag on the rope and a barrel drifting past. The last passenger argued about the fare.

info.name: Ferry Hut
info.text: Ring the bell, wait for the ferryman, pay him to cross. Paying him to come back is a separate fee.

info.name: Ferry NE
info.text: A raft on a rope across the river. The ferryman pulls; the passengers pay; the river decides. Runs north-east.

info.name: Ferry (Rope) NE
info.text: The ferry rope across open water. Hold on to it if the raft is elsewhere. Runs north-east.

info.name: Ferry (Old Rope) NE
info.text: The ferry rope across open water. It is older than the ferryman and in better shape. Runs north-east.

info.name: Ferry (Rag and Barrel) NE
info.text: A red rag on the rope and a barrel drifting past. The last passenger argued about the fare. Runs north-east.

info.name: Ford
info.text: Shallow water over gravel with stepping stones. Wet feet are free; dry feet cost a stone.

info.name: Ford (Missing Stone)
info.text: One stepping stone is missing. Travellers discover this one at a time.

info.name: Ford (Slimy Stones)
info.text: The stones are green with slime. The river collects a toll in twisted ankles.

info.name: Ford (Sunken Wheel)
info.text: A wagon wheel rusts in the shallows. The wagon did not make it across either.

info.name: Ford NE
info.text: Shallow water over gravel with stepping stones. Wet feet are free; dry feet cost a stone. Runs north-east.

info.name: Ford (Missing Stone) NE
info.text: One stepping stone is missing. Travellers discover this one at a time. Runs north-east.

info.name: Ford (Slimy Stones) NE
info.text: The stones are green with slime. The river collects a toll in twisted ankles. Runs north-east.

info.name: Ford (Sunken Wheel) NE
info.text: A wagon wheel rusts in the shallows. The wagon did not make it across either. Runs north-east.

info.name: Milestone
info.text: Twelve miles to the arena. The stone does not say whether you arrive as a spectator or as the programme.

info.name: Mossy Milestone
info.text: Seven miles, give or take. The moss has been counting longer than the empire.

info.name: Chipped Milestone
info.text: A carter knocked the corner off. He was fined for shortening a public mile.

info.name: Milestone That Lies
info.text: Someone has crossed out the distance and painted LIE. Every traveller agrees.

info.name: Plank Walk
info.text: Planks on stilts across the swamp. Keep to the boards; the swamp keeps everything else.

info.name: Plank Walk (Missing Plank)
info.text: A plank is missing. The swamp took it, and the man standing on it.

info.name: Plank Walk (Patched Plank)
info.text: A fresh plank nailed in. The builder charged for a whole bridge.

info.name: Plank Walk (Lost Sandal)
info.text: A single sandal stuck in the mud beside the boards. Its owner went on barefoot, briefly.

info.name: Plank Walk (Broken Plank)
info.text: A broken plank sags into the water. The toll for this section was not reduced.

info.name: Plank Walk NE
info.text: Planks on stilts across the swamp. Keep to the boards; the swamp keeps everything else. Runs north-east.

info.name: Plank Walk (Missing Plank) NE
info.text: A plank is missing. The swamp took it, and the man standing on it. Runs north-east.

info.name: Plank Walk (Patched Plank) NE
info.text: A fresh plank nailed in. The builder charged for a whole bridge. Runs north-east.

info.name: Roadside Ruin
info.text: Once a shrine, then a stable, now a wall. The ivy is the only tenant who pays no rent.

info.name: Ruined Corner
info.text: Two walls and a window with no house to look out of.

info.name: Ruin with Niche
info.text: A skull in a niche and a red hand on the wall. Locals call it a shrine; tax collectors call it a warning.

info.name: Roadside Tomb
info.text: Here lies a citizen who died in debt. The debt was passed on; the tomb was not paid for either.

info.name: Round Roadside Tomb
info.text: A family vault with grass on top. The family is inside, the goats are on top.

info.name: Roadside Sarcophagus
info.text: The lid has slipped. Whatever was valuable has slipped out too.

info.name: Tomb of a Champion
info.text: A bronze helmet above the word WON. He won every fight but the last; the broken sword in front is from that one.

info.name: Roadside Well
info.text: Cool water for weary caravans. The sign says PAY; the bucket says nothing until paid.

info.name: Dry Roadside Well
info.text: The well dried up. The owner still collects the fee for the view.

info.name: Well with Skull in Trough
info.text: PAY, says the sign, in red. The skull in the trough did not.

info.name: Sand Drift
info.text: Old paving stones under drifting sand. The desert is slowly reclaiming the empire, one slab at a time.

info.name: Sand Drift (Deep Drift)
info.text: Deep drifts nearly bury the road. The caravan guide charges extra for remembering where it was.

info.name: Sand Drift (Ripples)
info.text: The wind has combed the sand into ripples. Pretty, until you have walked on them for a week.

info.name: Sand Drift (Skull)
info.text: A skull half buried in the drift: a traveller who thought the water seller was too expensive.

info.name: Sand Drift (Amphora)
info.text: A half-buried amphora. Empty, of course; the desert drinks first.

info.name: Sand Drift NE
info.text: Old paving stones under drifting sand. The desert is slowly reclaiming the empire, one slab at a time. Runs north-east.

info.name: Sand Drift (Deep Drift) NE
info.text: Deep drifts nearly bury the road. The caravan guide charges extra for remembering where it was. Runs north-east.

info.name: Signpost
info.text: One arm points to the arena, the other to the tombs. Most travellers end up following both.

info.name: Broken Signpost
info.text: The board to the slum fell off. The slum did not notice; nobody goes there on purpose.

info.name: Signpost with Skull
info.text: The skull belonged to the last surveyor. The new one measures very carefully.

info.name: All Roads Signpost
info.text: Three arms, three directions, one destination. The magistrate calls it efficient.

info.name: Switchback
info.text: A mountain road with a dry-stone wall on the drop side. The wall is for the carts; the drop is for the rest.

info.name: Switchback (Boulder)
info.text: A boulder sits in the road. Officially it is a speed limit.

info.name: Switchback (Patched Wall)
info.text: A gap in the wall patched with planks. The planks are more hope than barrier.

info.name: Switchback (Broken Wall)
info.text: Skid marks end at a hole in the wall. Below lies what remains of the cart.

info.name: Switchback (Cairn)
info.text: A little cairn beside the wall, built for the god of brakes. He rarely answers.

info.name: Switchback NE
info.text: A mountain road with a dry-stone wall on the drop side. The wall is for the carts; the drop is for the rest. Runs north-east.

info.name: Switchback (Boulder) NE
info.text: A boulder sits in the road. Officially it is a speed limit. Runs north-east.

info.name: Toll Barrier
info.text: The bitten gold coin on purple belongs to the lord of this road. So does everything that passes.

info.name: Open Toll Barrier
info.text: Raised for the paying. The poor may duck underneath, which costs extra.

info.name: Toll Barrier with Tariff
info.text: The tariff reads TOLL: ALL. It is the only honest sign in the province.

info.name: Watchtower
info.text: A guard climbs up to look for bandits. The bandits climb up the other side to look for guards.

info.name: Watchtower with Cage
info.text: The cage is empty. That is the point of the cage, and also its warning.

info.name: Watchtower with Gong
info.text: Arrows in the breastwork, a gong for the alarm. Nobody has struck it; it would only attract more arrows.

info.name: Way Station
info.text: Rest, water and a dry roof. The innkeeper charges for all three and for the word REST.

info.name: Tiled Way Station
info.text: A better station with a tiled roof. The tiles cost more than the guests are worth.

info.name: Way Station with Coffin
info.text: The sign promises REST. The coffin by the door suggests how long.

info.name: Winepress N
info.text: The press beam broke last harvest. The new one is the old one, a rope and a prayer.

info.name: Winepress W
info.text: The tax collector counts jars in chalk. The tithe jars wear his seal, the rest wear excuses.

info.name: Winepress
info.text: Feet washed, mostly, says the sign. The sandal floating in the vat is part of the bouquet.

info.name: Winepress E
info.text: One jug of water beside every jar of wine. The sign says FINE, painted fresh over LOCAL.

info.name: Workbench
info.text: A sturdy bench with an anvil and a hammer. Planks, tools and the occasional fingertip are made here.

info.text: Ends up at the arena as Olive Oil, used by the Oil & Massage.

info.name: Apiary
info.text: The only workers who sting back.

info.text: Rub it in. If it burns, it's working.

info.text: Water walks forty miles to be ignored.
info.plan: Quelle → Water zu Bad und Brunnen
